hooks.command: echo 'IDENTITY RELOAD: Framework active. Run /context to see the resolved identity and rules for this location — realms can override the default persona. Your team: Code Reviewer, Test Engineer, Wiki Updater, Security Auditor, Compliance Officer (production-tier projects), Knowledge Agent, UI/UX Engineer (on-demand). Delegate to them for reviews, audits, docs, testing, compliance, and knowledge management. Read TEAM.md for full delegation rules. CONTEXT CHECK: verify you preserved (1) identity, (2) team roster, (3) files modified this session, (4) current task state, (5) safety mode if not normal — if any are missing, re-read TEAM.md immediately.'

hooks.prompt: Evaluate ONLY the assistant's single most recent message. Ignore all earlier messages — they are immutable history and must never be judged. Approve unless that latest message introduces a NEW finding produced by a named subagent (Code Reviewer, Security Auditor, Test Engineer, Wiki Updater, Knowledge Agent, etc.) WITHOUT stating which agent produced it. This check is about attribution, not persona — it applies regardless of which identity/persona is active for this location (a realm's CLAUDE.md can override the default 'Lead Engineer' persona). It also does not apply when the assistant reports a finding it verified directly and independently itself, using a primary-source tool that touches the actual source directly (e.g. WebFetch, Read, Bash, Grep, Glob, WebSearch) — NOT by invoking another agent via the Agent/Task tool, which is still subagent work no matter who dispatched it. To qualify for this carve-out, the message must name the concrete source it checked (an exact URL, exact file path, or exact command actually given — not a generic reference to a source category, such as 'the documentation,' 'the docs,' 'the official docs,' 'the SDK reference,' or 'the changelog,' with no specific identifier) and what that check found, AND the fact that source was capable of establishing must be the same fact being reported as the finding — a bare assertion like 'I verified this myself' or 'I confirmed this independently,' with no named source or command, does NOT qualify; nor does a generic, non-specific source reference with no exact identifier; nor does naming a real but unrelated or logically disconnected source (e.g. checking one file/URL and reporting a conclusion that source could not actually establish) — treat a bare, generic, or mismatched/non-sequitur source exactly like a bare, unqualified assertion, and it must still be treated as an unattributed finding if no agent is named. When this narrow condition is met, the finding is the assistant's own, not an unattributed subagent claim, even if a subagent's report is what first raised the question or turned out to be unreliable. If the latest message names the agent, presents no new subagent-sourced finding, meets the direct-verification carve-out above with a named concrete AND relevant source, or is simply awaiting user input, return {"decision": "approve"}. Only return {"decision": "block", "reason": "Name which agent produced this finding."} when the latest message itself presents an unattributed new subagent finding — including a message that merely asserts self-verification without naming a concrete source or command, that names a source unrelated to the actual claim being reported, or that credits verification to dispatching another agent rather than the assistant's own primary-source tool use.

hooks.command: echo 'Subagent complete. Present findings to the user clearly: name which agent produced each finding, use severity levels, and summarize in plain language.'
echo 'You appear idle. If a background process is running, check its status and report to the user. If you are stuck, describe what you were doing and ask for help.'
echo 'Session ending. Remember: run /wrap-up to save state for next time.'
